newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AKRAM IGNORES PAIN AS PAKISTAN CLINCH CUP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AKRAM IGNORES PAIN AS PAKISTAN CLINCH CUP.

text.p: Pakistan captain Wasim Akram shrugged off injury to spearhead a fast bowling rout of West Indies as his team clinched the World Series Cup on Monday.
The Pakistanis took the triangular limited overs competition for the first time after a decisive 62-run victory in the second match of the best-of-three final.
They made only a modest 165 in 48.3 of their 50 overs but dispatched West Indies for 103 in 40.3 overs, Akram providing the inspiration despite being restricted by a niggling hamstring injury.
Not even a power failure that left the stadium in darkness for 24 minutes could distract Pakistan from their task in taking an unassailable 2-0 lead in the final.
Akram dismissed opener Sherwin Campbell and middle order pair Shivnarine Chanderpaul and Carl Hooper in sweltering temperatures at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Pakistan's skipper was clearly troubled by the injury in the field but he still generated extreme pace, bounce and movement off the seam from a short run-up to take three for 17.

Fellow fast bowler Shahid Nazir, drafted into the side to replace leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed, justified his selection by exploiting a lively pitch to finish with outstanding figures of three for 14 from his 10 overs.
West Indies were 42 for seven at one stage and only some lusty blows by fast bowler Curtly Ambrose saved his side from greater embarrassment.
Ambrose, who went into the match with a groin strain and had to use a runner, hit an unbeaten 31, his highest score in a one-day international.
West Indies fast bowlers had posed their own problems earlier, captain Courtney Walsh, Ambrose and Cameron Cuffy sharing six wickets.
Cuffy ensured Pakistan opener Aamir Sohail did not last long on his return to the side from a one-match suspension for dissent by dismissing the hard-hitting left-hander for 16.
Ijaz Ahmed, top scorer in Pakistan's four-wicket victory in the opening game in Sydney on Saturday, scored 45 to bolster the middle order, while Mohammad Wasim hit 41 in the final overs off 79 balls.
Pakistan lifted the Cup for the first time in six attempts, earning $100,000 ($79,00) in prizemoney. Hosts Australia failed to make the finals.
